messages:
jia: Quick update from the longform bring-up: 14B-int8 shows a ~4.9% drop in QA F1 on the 'longform' eval (QA F1 fp16=0.742 -> int8=0.706) but unit cost/token drops ~2.5x (fp16 ~$0.42 per 1k tokens -> int8 ~$0.17). Median latency roughly same, p95 +80ms. Thoughts on rollout + guardrails?

eval-bot: automated-eval: longform_eval_v3 | samples=1,200 | qa_f1: fp16=0.742 | int8=0.706 | rougeL: fp16=0.591 | int8=0.578 | latency_ms_median: fp16=210 | int8=220 | latency_ms_p95: fp16=610 | int8=690 | cost_per_1k_tokens: fp16=$0.42 | int8=$0.17

ana: ugh that QA drop on long docs is notable. Where are errors coming from — hallucinations or missing context?

jia: Mostly missing contextual chains: the model trims salient evidence in multi-paragraph answers, leads to lower extractive match. Qualitative: shorter, confident answers that omit supporting spans. Not a hallucination spike.

ryan: For product recommendations I'd split by request length and criticality. Short q/a and low-risk flows -> int8. Longform/contract/legal -> fp16. Can we quantify a safe length threshold?

eva: On the longform set the distribution shows 65% of tokens > 3k. p95 length ~6.8k. If we route by length, need to ensure routing decision happens pre-tokenization to avoid extra cost.

mike: Proposed rollout plan: 1) Canary 1% traffic for non-critical endpoints for 48h. 2) A/B eval on longform bucket only with matched traffic for 72h. 3) If QA F1 delta <=1.5% and p95 latency < 750ms, increase to 10%. Otherwise rollback.

ryan: +1. Add a safety fallback: if model returns low answer length or low confidence (we're using a logit-based proxy), route that request to fp16 and mark for evaluation. Also keep a sampling of fp16 responses for quality monitoring while int8 is serving.

ana: Could we try selective kv-cache preservation / hybrid quant for long contexts? Maybe int8 for compute layers but keep top-K attention weights in fp16? Not trivial but worth microbenchmarking.

jia: Good idea. Also runs to try: (A) int8 + prefix caching (should help recall), (B) int8 but bump decoding beam/penalty hyperparams to favor coverage, (C) 14B-fp16 baseline. I'll schedule small eval runs.

eva: Ops checklist: routing rule prototype:
```
if request.tokens_estimate > 2048 or request.domain in ["legal","finance","contracts"]:
  route: redwood-14b-fp16
else:
  route: redwood-14b-int8
```
Make sure to instrument `route_reason` and sample 5% of int8 traffic back to fp16 for drift checks.

mike: Metric dashboards to add before canary: (1) QA F1 delta by length bucket (0-512,512-2k,2k-6k,6k+), (2) p95 latency by model, (3) inferred_confidence distribution, (4) cost per 1M tokens rolling.

ryan: Product note: recommend delaying exposure on paid SLAs until we have stable p95 and QA F1 within tolerance. For free-tier experiments it's fine to be aggressive. Keep GTN/CS in the loop if we change defaults.

jia: Action items: - run the three microbench variants (A,B,C) + qualitative triage (jia) - add routing prototype + route_reason logging (eva) - dash panels + alerts (mike) - canary policy + rollback thresholds doc (ryan) I'll open a tiny RFC with numbers.

ana: Thanks — if microbench shows hybrid-int8 recovers >2% F1 we can fast-track. Otherwise prefer conservative routing by length/domain. :thumbsup!
